concepts.title: Humidity, Evaporation and Relative Humidity
concepts.definition: Water in the atmosphere exists as vapour measured by absolute and specific humidity, and relative humidity compares the actual water vapour with the saturation vapour at that temperature as a percentage, so cooling air to its dew point saturates it and condensation begins.
concepts.key_idea: Relative humidity of 100 per cent means the air is saturated at the dew point temperature, when excess vapour condenses on nuclei into droplets.
question_patterns: define relative humidity and absolute humidity
calculate the relative humidity from actual and saturation vapour
what is the dew point temperature
how does evaporation depend on temperature and wind
why does warm air hold more moisture than cold air

solution_steps.explain: Divide the actual water vapour by the saturation vapour at the same temperature and multiply by 100 to get the relative humidity

concepts.title: Condensation, Clouds, Fog and Precipitation Types
concepts.definition: Condensation forms dew, frost, fog, mist and clouds when saturated air cools by expansion in convection, convergence or frontal and orographic lifting, and precipitation falls as rainfall, snowfall, sleet or hail when droplets grow heavy by Bergeron or collision-coalescence processes.
concepts.key_idea: Clouds are classified into cirrus, cumulus, stratus and their combinations by height and form, and orographic lifting gives heavy windward rainfall with rain shadow aridity behind.

concepts.title: Water Balance and the Importance of Atmospheric Moisture
concepts.definition: Atmospheric moisture links evaporation from oceans and lands with precipitation over land, forming the water balance that feeds rivers, lakes and groundwater, and the timing of this moisture delivery decides agriculture, water supply and flood risk.
concepts.key_idea: Only about one per cent of the hydrosphere is atmospheric water, yet it renews the entire land freshwater supply through continuous cycling.
